prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: desktop web first-viewport direction comp, 16:9 landscape
Primary request: Design a complete high-fidelity first screen for DOM X-Ray as an architectural museum-model inspection table. A recognizable flat webpage stands nearly front-on and peels into translucent measured layers; resource bytes become truthful physical mass and one external teal third-party hub sits beyond the page boundary. This must read as an interactive website result viewer, not a poster or concept-art scene.
Scene/backdrop: warm paper-and-board inspection table filling the browser with sparse graphite annotations at the edges
Subject: synthetic webpage cutaway with translucent drafting-film regions, stacked DOM depth, graphite outlines, one visibly weighted image region, exact red inspection callout, external teal machinery, and a hero fact tied to the selected region
Style/medium: award-quality editorial product UI mockup combining realistic museum-model materials with precise interface typography
Composition/framing: 1440x900-style desktop viewport; 3D cutaway owns right two-thirds; left third contains DOM X-RAY wordmark, synthetic URL input, X-RAY button, one-line hero fact, and compact provenance action; bottom edge carries Structure/Weight/Origins, Replay, and orbit hint; no top nav and no dashboard panels
Lighting/mood: quiet architectural model studio in soft daylight, exacting and tactile with a slightly mischievous red reveal
Color palette: warm paper #E9E1D2, graphite #20251F, inspection red #D9492F, external teal #2D6571, model board #B8AA8B
Materials/textures: translucent drafting film, graphite, inspection stamps, museum-model board, tiny engraved metal labels
Text (verbatim): "DOM X-RAY"; "example.com"; "X-RAY"; "THIS IMAGE CARRIED 61% OF THE TRANSFER"; "VIEW EVIDENCE"; "STRUCTURE"; "WEIGHT"; "ORIGINS"; "REPLAY"; "DRAG TO INSPECT DEPTH"; "SYNTHETIC PREVIEW"
Constraints: product purpose and primary action obvious within seconds; every dramatic object appears measurable; high contrast; clear focus states; no invented commercial claims
Avoid: generic dashboard, bento cards, neon, cyberpunk, glassmorphism, particles, floating KPI tiles, code editor, globe, roast language, speed score, decorative wires, excessive blur

approval.note: Approved by the user as the first-viewport composition. Treat spatial relationships as the implementation contract; all fixture copy remains dynamic scan data.
